rationale: There is direct evidence from a single case report (Yamada et al., 2023) showing that a de novo missense variant within the ATP-binding site (p.Gly414Arg) in DHX9 caused intellectual disability, short stature, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, with corresponding cardiac conduction defects recapitulated in heterozygous Dhx9 mutant mice. However, the hypothesis that cardiomyopathy defines a reproducible subset of ATP-binding domain DHX9 variants and distinguishes them from related helicase disorders is conflicted: (1) evidence in humans is restricted to an N of 1, with no replication across a larger cohort of ATP-binding variants; (2) cardiac non-compaction is also seen in animal models of related DExH-box helicases such as DHX36/RHAU (Yang et al., 2022), failing to demonstrate specificity for DHX9 over other helicases; and (3) the Dhx9 mouse model demonstrated cardiac conduction abnormalities rather than overt ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, showing phenotypic discordance between the human patient and animal model.

evidence.text: Yamada et al. (2023) identified a de novo heterozygous missense variant p.(Gly414Arg) in the glycine codon of the ATP-binding motif (G-C-G-K-T) of DHX9 in an individual presenting with intellectual disability, short stature, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy. Furthermore, heterozygous mice harboring the orthologous Dhx9 mutation (p.Gly416Arg) exhibited cardiac conduction abnormalities.

source.title: Heterozygous loss-of-function DHX9 variants are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders: Human genetic and experimental evidences
source.quote: Herein, we report a patients with a heterozygous de novo missense variant, p.(Gly414Arg) of DHX9 who presented with a short stature, intellectual disability, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy. The variant was located in the glycine codon of the ATP-binding site, G-C-G-K-T... Furthermore, in a gene-editing experiment of Dhx9 G416 to R416, corresponding to p.(Gly414Arg) in humans, heterozygous mice showed a reduced body size, reduced emotionality, and cardiac conduction abnormality.

evidence.text: Non-compaction cardiomyopathy has been linked to disruption of other DExH-box helicases such as RHAU (DHX36), demonstrating that cardiac non-compaction is not unique to DHX9 among related RNA/DNA helicase deficiencies.

conflicts: Ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy has only been reported in 1 patient with a DHX9 ATP-binding site variant (p.Gly414Arg); there is currently no cohort data establishing this as a consistent or recurring sub-phenotype for ATP-binding domain variants.

Dhx9 mutant mice (p.Gly416Arg) exhibited cardiac conduction abnormalities rather than structural ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, leaving the exact cardiac phenotype of DHX9 ATP-binding disruption unresolved.

Non-compaction cardiomyopathy is also produced by deficiency of related DExH-box helicase family members such as DHX36 (RHAU), conflicting with the claim that it specifically distinguishes DHX9 from other helicase-related pathologies.

new_directions.question_text: In comprehensive DHX9 patient cohorts (such as those with Charcot-Marie-Tooth and neurodevelopmental disorder phenotypes), what is the systematically evaluated prevalence of ventricular non-compaction and cardiac conduction defects across different functional domains?
new_directions.rationale: A single patient report cannot establish a domain-specific genotype-phenotype correlation; routine echocardiography and electrocardiography across broader DHX9 patient cohorts are needed to test whether cardiomyopathy is recurrent in ATP-binding variants or merely a private/incidental finding.

new_directions.question_text: Do Dhx9 G416R mutant mice develop histological or ultrastructural features of ventricular non-compaction under physiological cardiac stress or advanced age?
new_directions.rationale: Yamada et al. identified conduction abnormalities in mutant mice, but detailed assessment of myocardial trabeculation and compaction ratios would clarify whether the mouse model recapitulates the structural human cardiomyopathy.
